the words-only rule is expressible with what exists: a passive or an unnamed duty keeps its bearer out of the language. A prohibition ('No one shall be held in slavery') is a permission predicate over the thing itself (the holding) refused by the rule; a duty ('shall be made available') is an obligation over the thing with no bearer argument; 'has the right to X' is the entitlement (a plain predicate), the liberty (a permission) and claims that say, of no stated party, what must hold of every person. VE reports such a case SETTLED and every other case UNDECIDED, and says nothing about any State, group or person

a limit that remains: an obligation's act phrase is 80 bytes with no 'and', 'not', 'or', 'for', 'no' or 'is' and no comma, and an English-view noun may not hold 'the' or 'and'. The combined (noninterference plus securing) reading of nine long rights is therefore a claim over a sort of right holders (persons) whose name is the right's topic and whose description carries the source's whole phrase; a plain obligation over the person cannot carry the phrase twice

the status witnesses of the companions are Lean's rows since lf-10b: the previous Python `situation`/`status` objects no longer exist, and witnesses_nd.py reads `norm-defaults-status` (enumerate, then the `undecided` replay) through the public route

limits unchanged and still blocking: act-phrase grammar (11 units), time (5), causation (4), comparison (2), quantities (1), grounding of authority (1), priority of rights (1), right_lines across open sets (4), attribution, modality/belief, evaluative claims; defaults beside soft norms (u017); none of these moved

words_only.rule: lead, 2026-10-08: a reading set is allowed only where the English itself supports more than one meaning; no reading from outside knowledge (who usually bears a duty); outside knowledge only in an unchecked note
